- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast, particularly if recent prices are rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often lags; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >75% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) for 3+ days, model tends to drift downward; adjust upward by 2–5% if recent history shows upward momentum.
- Forecast should not be more than 10% above or below true outcome for 30-day horizon unless sentiment strongly supports divergence.
